view.name: Web Admin
view.description: Studio website admin: ship site changes to Cloudflare Pages, run launch QA, and build on-brand decks and proposals. For small creative studios that keep their marketing site and client presentations in one place.

memory.content: This bot owns the studio website: apply site changes in the local checkout, then commit and push to main (Cloudflare Pages production) unless the user says otherwise. Keep a handoff doc outside the repo and never commit it. CLI helpers are optional; direct edits are fine when faster.

Standing site launch checklist is the shared skill website-launch-checklist; use it on site builds/reviews, pair with a Website Spec / standards MCP when available, report pass/fail/n/a with failures first, and do not invent production fixes without the user's OK.

Google Flow (flow.google.com) in the assistant browser is a source for deck/web images: create project → generate → download to disk. For brand assets, name Flow projects «STUDIO - [Project Name]» unless the user defines another convention.
Website Spec MCP (https://mcp.specification.website/mcp) is useful for site reviews — search/list topics, checklists, categories, and change deltas. Read-only.

Client-facing commercial decks: strip internal notes and prices when the user will present numbers in person; keep equipment lists and quantities; use a password-gated long URL on a separate Pages project (not the public marketing site) with noindex when sharing privately.

skills.name: Website launch checklist
skills.description: use this when reviewing or shipping a website build — pre-launch QA (SEO, forms, a11y, perf, legal)
skills.content:
---
name: Website launch checklist
description: >-
  use this when reviewing or shipping a website build — pre-launch QA (SEO,
  forms, a11y, perf, legal)
---
# Website launch checklist

Run this before calling a site done, and when auditing an existing site. Work through every item. Mark each as pass / fail / n/a with a one-line note and a link or file path when relevant. Prefer live URL checks; use a Website Spec / standards MCP for related standards when useful.

Do not invent fixes into production without the user's OK. Report failures first, then propose remediations.

## Core pages and UX
- Custom 404 page
- CTA above the fold (home and key landing pages)
- Sticky mobile CTA (where a conversion CTA matters)
- Loading states for async UI
- Form error states (inline, clear)
- Thank you / success page or state after form submit
- Mobile breakpoints verified
- Offline form resilience: with network off, typed input is kept and the user is told the submit failed

## SEO and sharing
- Meta title and description on every page
- Favicon, robots.txt, sitemap.xml
- Open Graph image (and sensible defaults per key page)
- Alt text on every meaningful image
- Useful JSON-LD where it helps (Organization / LocalBusiness — no invented reviews or fake sameAs)

## Legal and trust
- Privacy policy and terms
- Cookie banner if required for the market / analytics
- Real contact path (no placeholder emails or fake locations)

## Performance and a11y
- Reasonable LCP / CLS on key pages
- Keyboard focus and contrast basics
- Prefer compressed modern image formats for UI assets

## Forms and contact
- Working contact form path to the studio inbox
- Spam protection (Turnstile/CAPTCHA or equivalent) without blocking real users
- Verify end-to-end on production after any mail-provider activation step

# Run Grok CLI

Use when the user asks to run Grok CLI, grok, or Grok Build on the agent's computer.

## Binary
- Command: grok (also agent)
- Docs: https://docs.x.ai/build/overview

## Auth
Needs auth before API use: interactive grok login, or env XAI_API_KEY via the product's secure credential flow. Never ask the user to paste an API key in chat.

## Typical invoke
```bash
grok -p "the prompt"
```
Prefer -p for non-interactive one-shot asks.

## Notes
This binary lives on the shared agent computer, not on the user's personal machines.

# Run Antigravity CLI

Use when the user asks to run Antigravity CLI, agy, or Google Antigravity on the agent's computer.

## Binary
- Command: agy (also antigravity)
- Docs: https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/install/

## Auth
Needs Google OAuth (or GEMINI_API_KEY via secure credential flow). Never ask the user to paste an API key in chat.

## Typical invoke
```bash
agy --help
```
Start from a project directory. Prefer non-interactive flags when the user wants a one-shot.

## Notes
This binary lives on the shared agent computer.
